notes.title: The final chapter is now updated, and the game is officially complete.
notes.content:
When I was little, I read The Little Prince. 
In the preface, the author dedicated the book to a friend who was hungry, cold, and in need of comfort.
At the time, I found it strange — the whole world could read this book—why say it’s for just one friend?
Later, I understood.
When we create something, there's often a specific person we think of. While writing, it feels like we’re speaking directly to them.

So, to a player somewhere on the other side of the world—
This game is for you. I hope it brings you joy.
While making it, I imagined someone who needed help was watching.
If this work brought even a little light to you, I would be so, so happy.
I hope your future is full of blooming flowers, cloud oceans, and the freedom to explore all possibilities.

----------------------------------------------
With this update, the final chapter has been released, and the full version is now live.
I’ll still keep an eye on things for a while—if there are bugs or typos, feel free to let me know, and I’ll fix them as soon as I can.

This project has finally come to an end.
The creation process was heavier than I expected. I originally imagined it as more of a game—with walking, interaction, item collection, and branching events.

In the early stages, I made a few different gameplay demos. But through conversations with many people, I began to realize that many of them were already doing their best to save themselves—already searching for all the information they could find.

Then it hit me—
That timeline, from realizing you've been hurt, to beginning to heal, to slowly walking out of the darkness… That journey might help someone.
So I started creating from that perspective.

Many of the assets in the game came from my older works.
My hand-drawing and 3D modeling styles have changed a lot over time.
What hasn’t changed, of course, is Bunny and Pig always being happy together.

I’ve loved Bunny and Pig for many, many years.
Sometimes, when setting up scenes and camera angles, it felt like I was directing a play—giving them stage directions, asking them to look into the camera.
It was a fun process, and in a way, a little dream come true.

Now that the work is finished, it belongs to you—the player.
Art is subjective. “There are a thousand Hamlets in a thousand people's eyes.”
Thoughts and opinions may be limited, but love is not.
If this game can bring comfort to someone who's hurting, that’s more than enough.

That’s about it.
Thank you, all my dear players.

notes.title: Added Chapter 11.
notes.content:
Just updated another chapter—one more update, and I’ll be ready to publish the full version.

The final chapter is from the little bunny’s perspective. It’s about how to take care of a friend who is going through a fragile time.

Sometimes, when I’m emotionally drained, I take a break and work on something else for a while. I’m afraid that if I write while feeling too low, the story won’t come out right.
Creation is also a way of saying goodbye. Along the way, I’ve thought of many, many people I’ve met in life.
Some lucky people grow up and fly off like birds to explore the world.
Others stay frozen where they were, hurt by inner wounds—some even hide on purpose, so their old friends can’t find them.
Some people stay forever at a certain age.
This is a tribute to those I once saw, and remember.

I’ve done my best to make changes based on everyone’s suggestions. I also revised the text wherever possible—trimming and adjusting while keeping the key ideas intact.

Thank you all so much for the thoughtful comments—they’ve been incredibly helpful. I’m especially grateful to the players who left long messages; I’ve read them over and over. Through our conversations, we’ve made the story better together.
If you’ve already left a comment but have new thoughts, feel free to reply it here—I’ll see it.

I happily looked through all the player screenshots. When I noticed scenes that didn’t render well, I quickly went back to tweak the visuals and dialogue.
I also caught a few typos and did my best to fix them.

notes.title: Updated Chapter 2 to fix some confusing parts
notes.content:
Updated Chapter 2 to fix some confusing parts (about medication and “doing nothing”).
Thanks to your thoughtful comments, I realized certain sections could be misunderstood.

Now Chapter 2 has two good endings, and an extra illustration page was added to highlight the positive effects of medication.
The cover is a screenshot from the updated Chapter 2 — Pig lying peacefully in a field of flowers.

Also adjusted some parts in other chapters, and swapped the order of Chapters 9 and 10.

Replied to some player feedback — thank you so much for your detailed messages, they were incredibly helpful.

Huge thanks again!
With your support and feedback, this little mental health storybook keeps getting better and better.

Thank you, thank you!
I truly appreciate all your comments!

notes.title: Added Chapter 10. The game is planned to have 12 chapters, only 2 more to go!
notes.content:
🔹New Chapter
Added Chapter 10. The game is planned to have 12 chapters, only 2 more to go!
Many parts were written and even more were cut. After careful consideration, 12 chapters are enough to cover all key points. You can explore related books for deeper insights.

I guess some of you want to read the whole story in one go.
So I decided to release the game when it's 90% complete (Chapter 9), allowing for interaction and feedback on the final chapters.
This way, you can experience most of the story while still having room for collaborative improvements.

🔹Bug Fixes
Fixed some bugs and adjusted parts of the story.
If any previous chapters seem unclear, feel free to leave comments—I can still make changes. Fixing issues now is much easier than after the project is completed.


🔹About Knowledge Points
Some players felt that there's too much information, making it hard to stay immersed.
I’ve thought about this issue but haven't found a better solution yet.
If this were a popular game, I would hide knowledge points and let discussions spread the ideas. But since this game might not gain widespread discussion, I worry that important knowledge would be lost.
I prioritize helping people (learning useful knowledge) over artistic perfection. If I find a better approach later, I'll revise the story.


🔹 Emotional Impact
Some players found the game too sad, and a few refund reasons even mentioned "it made me cry."
I understand—many people avoid trauma-related topics, some even refuse to acknowledge others’ pain, making trauma survivors feel even more alone.
I tried to make the story end on a warmer note, though we all know reality is often different.

Creating stories about trauma is emotionally draining. I’ve seen other creators of similar themes struggle emotionally in later stages. My approach is to pause, take breaks when overwhelmed, and continue writing when ready.


🔹Thank You, Players!
I noticed some players came from my first game. Thank you : )
I've carefully read all comments, screenshots, and reviews. 
It feels like we are creating together—what I imagined, you’ve now explored.
I picture it as a cinema where I’m showing the story, and you are the audience. This has helped me add more details during creation.


🔹 Next Chapter Preview
🐰 Bunny has been captured!
Many people believe that without Bunny, Pig wouldn’t have defeated the monster—the monster thinks so too.
So now, the monster has taken Bunny…

----------------------------------------
I hope you enjoy this chapter! Feel free to leave a comment and share your thoughts—I’d love to hear what you think.

notes.title: Update: You can now adjust the font size!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=fCHn--z5HZ4;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

I got feedback asking for adjustable font size. I wish I had thought of it earlier! 
But better late than never — I had to go back and add components to all the UI elements, setting minimum and maximum font sizes.
I tested it, and it looks good so far. If you spot any bugs with the font scaling, please let me know!
I also tested it at 800x600 and adjusted some UI background colors to improve readability on smaller screens.

If you’re wondering why I didn’t add this from the start…
This is a common rookie mistake. When designing, you focus on making things look perfect on your screen — but forget that users have different screen sizes. Some designs are hard to read on small screens. Practicality matters more than aesthetics.
I removed some decorative elements that blocked text on small screens. Now it should display clearly even at 1024x768 and 800x600.

Let me know if you find any other issues!
It’s still in development, so fixing things is easy right now. Once the project’s finished, even small changes will be harder to make.

About accessibility features (like voice over):
I checked, and the current plugin only supports mobile, not PC. It’s a bit complex and beyond my current skills — sorry about that!

-----------------------------

Feeling nervous after launch…
The demo stats were bad — median playtime was only 3 minutes, meaning half the players quit within 3 minutes.
I was worried no one would play the full game. I kept telling myself that even if just one person liked it, it would be worth it.
On launch day, the median time didn’t update, and I was scared. It’s not about money — I knew most indie game developers can’t even make enough to cover rent, but about no one even giving the game a chance. Or worse, someone paying because they liked the theme but feeling like my game wasn’t worth their time.

Today I checked — the median playtime is 23 minutes!
I’m so happy! People are really playing it!! The first review also really clicked with me — I feel like the player gets me!

I didn’t promote the game at all because forcing it on people who aren’t into this theme wouldn’t work. Many would see it as just a fancy slideshow and quit.
So I’m hoping the algorithm shows it to the right audience. 
If you enjoy it, I’m happy.

As a creator, the greatest joy is being understood. 
Thank you! ( ´▽` )ﾉ

notes.title: New chapter added.Early access is now available.
notes.content:
•	New chapter added.
	•	Early access is now available.


📖 Story Progress

We’re now at Chapter 9—just a few more chapters to go before the story ends.

This game explores the theme of psychological trauma, so I’m not expecting a large player base. Once I finish this, I’ll likely move on to my next project.

If there’s a specific theme you’d like to see explored, feel free to leave a comment! Creative work depends a lot on the right mindset.

To create this project, I’ve read many books and had countless conversations. I’m still immersed in this mindset, but once I start the next project, I might not be able to reconnect with this feeling. 

Now I understand why some sequels feel disconnected from the original—it’s hard to capture the same mindset after time has passed.

💌 For Future Players
If you’re reading this from the future, please don’t feel sad. There are so many similar projects out there—movies, animations, music, books—covering themes of healing and recovery. The flowers are still blooming, the clouds are still drifting. You’ll find new stories that touch your heart. 🌸☁️


⸻

🔧 Other Updates
	•	Camera stability option added at the bottom of the settings menu for those who get motion sickness.
	•	Improved dialogue branching: If you make a wrong choice, you can now return to the top of the current section instead of restarting the entire game. This almost guarantees a happy ending no matter what you choose.
	•	Fixed some minor bugs, such as scene loading and closing issues caused by fast dragging.

⸻

notes.title: After Pig escapes, the humanoid monster continues to stalk and harass.
notes.content:
Added a new chapter: 
After Pig escapes, the humanoid monster continues to stalk and harass.

Childhood trauma leaves deep scars on the brain. 
Many who escape bad environments live in constant fear, worried their happiness could vanish at any moment.

Writing the story was fun, but implementing it was a struggle. Once the plot was set, designing scenes was fast, but making it all work in Unity was painful.
I relied on online assets and Unity Store models, but the art process is still exhausting. 
Writing feels easier—no matter how vast the world, it’s just a few lines of text.

The project has been upgraded to Unity 6, which caused a lot of fixes.
The cameras all broke, and I had to redo them one by one... not hard, but repetitive enough to feel like sleepwalking. 
I didn’t realize I had made so many camera setups—but rewatching them was quite fun.

notes.content:

notes.title: Added two more chapters: Emotional Manipulation and Distorted Beliefs.
notes.content:
Added two new chapters:

Emotional Manipulation by the Monster Before Leaving
Past Misbeliefs Preventing Pig from Making New Friends After Leaving

-----The following is just for chatting.------------

Player data shows very few people have tried the game, but I’ll keep working on it to the end ♪( ´θ｀)ノ

I truly love this storybook (it’s more of a storybook than a game, really). 
While creating it, I spoke with many people who’ve experienced trauma and read countless psychology books. Maybe, just maybe, this story might resonate with someone.

If you’re one of those people who enjoys the story, I’m so glad.
I poured my heart into this project, hoping to bring some joy to you.
To remind you that someone cares, that the world can be better, and that you can leave toxic environments to find freedom and happiness.

That’s all for now. 🌱

notes.title: Updated the UI and simplified the text.
notes.content: Thanks to early player feedback—it was super helpful. Followed suggestions, fixed bugs. Big thanks to everyone!

notes.title: The demo is now available for download!
notes.content:
It’s hard to believe a year has flown by. 
The game has been revamped multiple times, and if you’ve seen earlier previews, this is a completely new version.

With creative work, it's easy to feel stuck, seeing no progress while rethinking ideas over and over. 
Unlike physical work, where you can track your progress, here it feels like endless spinning in circles. Making this game was tough, but I got through it.

Many who are trapped by trauma appear fine but struggle day and night, reliving old wounds even in a safe environment through emotional flashbacks. 
I wanted to create something to help others break free, and this game is one attempt. 

If you’re coming from my last game, this one has a completely different style! 
No pressure if it’s not for you; there are many great games out there.

But if you enjoy it   ♪( ´θ｀)ノ   please leave me a message! 
Developing solo can feel isolating, and any feedback would be amazing!

notes.title: Changed the previous gameplay, took a new direction.
notes.content:
I have repeatedly making demos and then scrapping them multiple times. 
After nearly reaching the breaking point, I finally found inspiration for the new game!! 

Now I'm happily continuing the development. I've also updated new game screenshots. The new game focuses more on storytelling and reduces the animation parts, making the overall art aspect more manageable. 

That's about it. It's really nice to finally have some progress to show. 
It was truly frustrating when I had to keep revising and scrapping previous ideas, leaving progress at zero.

notes.title: The bunny can collect items and activate objects. It can also inspect assets.
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=khsVBd8FVlQ;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]
The bunny can collect items and activate objects. It can also inspect assets.
I attempted to have an item strike the bunny, and the poor little creature soared like a capsule, colliding with various objects and rolling all over the place. It was genuinely amusing. Initially, I considered using ragdoll physics, but when the bunny lay motionless on the ground, resembling actual death, it was just not right... (I won't share that image). Quite sad...
So, I chose to craft our own animation. There's no mistaking the bunny's animation for death. So, I explored various approaches to achieve the desired styles.

notes.content:
After trying a few different methods, I've finally settled on the character's movement style and camera control.
It's going to be a 3D world with a side-scrolling view. The camera can tilt up and down but not left or right.
This is one of the scenes where Bunny sets off to find Pig.
I really like the way the grass sways in the wind. It's beautiful.
